conventions.convention: The metric is diag(-1,1,1,1), sigma⁰=I₂, P₀=-P⁰, and natural units have ħ=c=1. Charges have actual Hilbert adjoints and share an invariant product domain containing the vacuum vector.

A vacuum is a normalized rest-frame ground-state vector. Its energy is an eigenvalue, not an energy density. Supersymmetry invariance requires annihilation by every charge and its adjoint; boundary neutrality is a separately defined predicate.
The component-bound equality case requires both y=0 and x≥0, under r≥0 and r²=x²+y².

The minimization ranges over ordinary complex bosonic pointwise values, with canonical Kähler metric, k,m≠0 and arbitrary y. It does not order nilpotent coefficients or establish admissible homogeneous spacetime vacua under compact-support conditions.
The ATLAS exclusion plane uses the chargino–LSP splitting δ± and fixes the neutralino splitting δ₀=2δ±; classifier parameter values refer to δ₀.
Reported 95% exclusions use source-specific asymptotic CLs procedures and benchmark spectra; they are neither posterior model probabilities nor general exact-coverage assertions.

load_bearing.statement: A rest-frame ground-state vector Ω belongs to the common product domain, has norm one, satisfies P⁰Ω=EΩΩ and PʲΩ=0, and obeys ⟨P⁰ψ,ψ⟩≥EΩ‖ψ‖² for every ψ∈D(P⁰). Supersymmetry invariance means every charge and its actual adjoint annihilates Ω.
For x,y,r∈ℝ with r≥0 and r²=x²+y², one has x≤r. Equality holds exactly when y=0 and x≥0.

published_dependencies.used_for: Ordered-field positivity, trichotomy, square comparisons, and characteristic zero in the component-bound and minimization proofs.
The explicitly inherited ACω assumption of the positive-unitary representation setup.
Unique complex coordinates, division by nonzero parameters, absence of zero divisors, and the exact count of square roots.
Definitions of conjugation, real and imaginary parts, and nonnegative modulus.
Definiteness and multiplicativity of modulus and conjugation identities throughout the potential minimization.
Existence of the nonzero roots realizing the second minimization regime.
Operational measurement and calibration terminology in both search reports.
Likelihoods as functions of parameters for specified dominated sampling families, without interpreting them as parameter probabilities.
Rejection-region and sampling-error terminology in the experimental analyses.
Frequentist coverage terminology and the distinction between coverage and posterior model probability.

concerns.concern: Procedure, paragraph beginning “For 1ℓ1T”, defines: “A fake track is one that passes the candidate selection but is not a prompt lepton from the signal decay.” This includes genuine prompt leptons from Standard Model backgrounds, contradicting the report's subsequent separation and subtraction of true-lepton backgrounds. The [ATLAS paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.20042v2), §7.2, printed pp. 22–23, distinguishes fake leptons from real-lepton tracks, including Z(*)+jets and diboson backgrounds; membership is not defined by whether the lepton originated in the hypothesized signal. The definition as written misstates the background categories.

Setup calls the benchmark “R-parity conserving” without defining R-parity or identifying an exact earlier definition. The four declared prerequisites define statistical concepts only. Give the relevant discrete charge and conservation convention, or a precise supplier, so this physical applicability qualification is defined rather than merely named.

Setup distinguishes “R-parity-conserving (RPC)” and “R-parity-violating (RPV)” benchmarks and names an RPV λ′ interaction, but supplies no mathematical definition of R-parity or the indicated interaction. The declared statistical prerequisites do not define either. State the relevant charge/conservation convention and interaction content, or identify exact earlier definitions, while retaining the explicitly source-limited branching assumptions.
